title: Bring your ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini history · {name}
description: Move your ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini conversations into an AI that keeps them on your computer: export them there, drop the file here, nothing comes in twice.
lede: Years of conversations in ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini? Export them there, drop the file in {name}, and they come in: every conversation with its title and dates, projects with their instructions, nothing twice. Then use any AI, those included.
pane.head: Brought in
pane.rows: Trip to Lisbon, day by day
Cover letter for the bakery job
how.title: Export it where it is.
how.why: Each app gives you your history as a file, sent by email. {name} reads that file as it comes.
how.cards: In ChatGPT: Settings › Data controls › Export data.
A link to a .zip arrives by email. Drop that file in {name} as it is.
In Claude, on the web or the desktop app: Settings › Privacy › Export data. On a Team or Enterprise plan, an owner allows it first.
A link arrives by email and works for 24 hours. Drop the file in {name} as it is.
At takeout.google.com: Deselect all, tick Gemini for your Gems, and My Activity with Gemini Apps alone. Choose JSON as My Activity’s format: {name} doesn’t read its web pages.
A link to a .zip arrives by email, within hours or days. Drop it in {name} as it is.
how.then: Then, in {name}: {settings} › {data} › {restore}, or drop the file in the box. Several exports come in one after the other.
what.title: What comes in, and what doesn’t.
what.why: {name} brings in what was said and what you shared. What another app’s tools did has no place in an answer here.
what.ins: Every conversation, with its title and its dates.
Where you edited a request or tried an answer again, the version you saw last.
Claude’s projects and Gemini’s Gems, with their instructions and their documents.
Nothing twice: bring the same export again and nothing is doubled.
Files you shared with ChatGPT or Gemini; from Claude, the text Claude read in them.
what.outs: What the tools did and what the AI thought: searches, code it ran, ChatGPT’s canvases, Claude’s artifacts, its reasoning.
Pictures ChatGPT made, and pictures you gave Claude: its export leaves them out.
A conversation that grew since you brought it in: it isn’t brought in again.
Which Claude project a conversation belonged to: the export doesn’t say.
never.title: Then, never move again.
never.why: What you bring in stays yours, in a form any app can read, with whichever AI you choose next.
never.cards: Each conversation is a file of its own, in an open format, kept encrypted on your computer by {name}.
Carry on with the AI on your computer, a free one, your key or your plan, and switch from the box, request by request.
Keep a copy of everything in one file, and restore it on any device.
never.compare: {name} beside the AI apps you know
limits.title: What to know first.
limits.items: The export is made by the other app, which emails a link: from minutes to a few days.
Gemini’s activity must be in JSON; its web pages don’t come in.
Your history stays in the other app too, until you delete it there.
A very large export takes longer to read on a slow computer.
faq.title: Your questions.
faq.items: Do I have to close my ChatGPT account?
No. Exporting changes nothing there. Keep both, or use ChatGPT’s AI from {name} with your plan, on a computer.
Does my history go to a server?
No. {name} reads the export on your computer and keeps what it brings in there, encrypted. Nothing reaches us.
Can I bring in several apps?
Yes, one export after the other, into the project you’re in.
Will I find an old conversation?
Yes: search finds conversations as you type, part of a word enough, in any language.
Yes. Bringing your history in costs nothing, and neither does {name}.
I exported a while ago. Can I use that file?
Yes, if it is ChatGPT’s or Claude’s .zip, or Gemini’s Takeout in JSON. Bring a newer one later: what is already here doesn’t come in twice.
end.title: Bring your history, then choose your AI.
end.why: {name} opens on Your data, ready for the file. Nothing to install.
